title: 30-year mortgage rate eases to 7.18%, third weekly decline
summary: Freddie Mac's weekly survey put the average 30-year fixed rate at 7.18% on November 5, down from 7.24% a week earlier but up from 6.22% a year ago.
body: The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate fell to 7.18% in Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey for the week of November 5, 2026, down from 7.24% the week before. It was the third weekly decline in a row.

The 15-year fixed rate averaged 6.57%, down from 6.60% the prior week. A year earlier the two rates were 6.22% and 5.50%, so borrowing is still about a percentage point more expensive than in late 2025.
Freddie Mac's survey reports national averages for conventional, conforming loans. Individual quotes depend on credit, down payment and loan type.

quote.text: Mortgage rates continued their downward trajectory this week

why: A few tenths of a point changes the payment on every financed deal. On a $280,000 loan over 30 years, the drop from 7.24% to 7.18% lowers principal and interest by roughly $11 a month. Re-run your numbers in the mortgage payment calculator and the cash flow calculator with this week's rate.
source_name: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey
